title: Unique By First Name
statement:
Return one directory entry for each first name.

Contract
- `people` is non-null. Each entry has a non-blank `first` and `last` name.
- Return a new list sorted by first name ascending. If several entries share a first name, keep the one that appeared earliest in the input.
- Do not mutate the input list.

Examples
- `uniqueByFirstName([Ada Lovelace, Bob Stone, Ada Byron])` returns `[Ada Lovelace, Bob Stone]`.
- `uniqueByFirstName([Zoe Zed, Amy Able, Zoe Young])` returns `[Amy Able, Zoe Zed]`.
- `uniqueByFirstName([])` returns `[]`.
hints: Track the first entry seen for each first name before thinking about order.
After duplicates are removed, only the remaining entries need to be sorted by first name.
A linked map plus a final sort gives the intended O(n log n) time and O(n) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: first:last pairs separated by spaces, for example: Ada:Lovelace Bob:Stone Ada:Byron
